en: Dependent on a phenomenon that is non-reactive and non-demonstrable, a phenomenon that is reactive and demonstrable arises by way of root condition … one.
Dependent on a phenomenon that is non-reactive and non-demonstrable, a phenomenon that is reactive and demonstrable arises by way of root condition … one.
[Dependent on] a phenomenon that is both non-reactive and non-demonstrable, and a phenomenon that is non-reactive and non-demonstrable … [and so forth].

Dependent on a phenomenon that is with resistance (*sappaṭigha*) and visible-with-resistance (*sanidassana-sappaṭigha*), a phenomenon that is with resistance and visible-with-resistance arises by way of the root condition (*hetu-paccaya*).

... [one]. (In all cases, there are three. Under the root condition, there are three; under the predominance condition, there are three... up to ... under the non-disappearance condition, there are three.

Dependent on a phenomenon that is neither with resistance nor visible-with-resistance (*nasappaṭigha-na-anidassana-sappaṭigha*), a phenomenon that is with resistance and invisible-with-resistance (*sappaṭigha-anidassana-sappaṭigha*) arises by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated. Under the root condition, there is one; under the predominance condition, there is one... up to ... under the non-disappearance condition, there is one.

Dependent on a state that is non-reactive and non-demonstrable, there arises a state that is non-reactive and non-demonstrable by way of root condition. (Abbreviated. One [condition] in the case of root; one in the case of predominance …pe… one in the case of non-disappearance.
